claim: HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer accounts for approximately 70% of all breast cancer.
source: Hormone receptor (HR)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer is the most prevalent subtype of breast cancer, which accounts for approximately 70% of all breast cancer (Parker et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Parker et al., 2009

claim: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy is recommended as the first choice for patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer who are candidates for preoperative therapy according to NCCN guidelines.
source: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NCT) is recommended as the first choice for patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer, who are candidates for preoperative therapy, according to National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guidelines (Gradishar et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to NCCN guidelines (Gradishar et al., 2022)

claim: Neoadjuvant endocrine therapy is an acceptable, less toxic alternative to neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
source: Neoadjuvant endocrine therapy (NET) is an acceptable, less toxic alternative to NCT.
evidence: Based on established clinical knowledge about treatment alternatives

claim: Less than 10% of patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer can achieve pathological complete response with neoadjuvant chemotherapy or endocrine therapy.
source: However, less than 10% of patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer can achieve pathological complete response (pCR), and only 60% of patients respond to NCT or NET (Sella et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sella et al., 2021

claim: Only 60% of patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer respond to neoadjuvant chemotherapy or endocrine therapy.
source: However, less than 10% of patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer can achieve pathological complete response (pCR), and only 60% of patients respond to NCT or NET (Sella et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sella et al., 2021

claim: CDK4/6 inhibitors have remarkable efficacy in the advanced setting when combined with endocrine therapy for HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.
source: Cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) inhibitors are breakthroughs in the treatment of HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer and have a remarkable efficacy in the advanced setting when combined with endocrine therapy (ET) (Finn et al., 2015; Goetz et al., 2017; Hortobagyi et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Finn et al., 2015; Goetz et al., 2017; Hortobagyi et al., 2016

claim: Abemaciclib has been approved for high-risk, early HR-positive breast cancer plus endocrine therapy as adjuvant treatment.
source: Presently, abemaciclib has been approved for high-risk, early HR-positive breast cancer plus ET as adjuvant treatment, and its application is being explored in the neoadjuvant setting (neoMONARCH and NCT04293393).
evidence: Based on established knowledge of drug approvals

claim: Therapies with a combination of CDK4/6 inhibitors and neoadjuvant endocrine therapy only achieve a pCR rate of less than 5%.
source: However, therapies with a combination of CDK4/6 inhibitors and NET only achieve a pCR rate of less than 5% (Hurvitz et al., 2020; Johnston et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hurvitz et al., 2020; Johnston et al., 2019

claim: In the PALLET study, objective response rate was not statistically significantly different between combinational therapy and monotherapy (54.3% vs 49.5%, p=0.20).
source: In the PALLET study, objective response rate (ORR) was not statistically significantly different between the combinational therapy and monotherapy (54.3% vs 49.5%, p=0.20; Johnston et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Johnston et al., 2019 with specific data

claim: In the FELINE study, there was no statistical difference in clinical, mammographic, ultrasound, or MRI response between letrozole alone and combination of letrozole with a CDK4/6 inhibitor.
source: Likewise, in the FELINE study, there was no statistical difference in clinical, mammographic, ultrasound, or MRI response between letrozole alone and combination of letrozole with a CDK4/6 inhibitor (Khan et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Khan et al., 2020

claim: Radiotherapy controls malignancy by breaking DNA in tumor cells.
source: Radiotherapy is one of the most important local methods to control malignancy by breaking DNA in tumor cells (Cox and Swanson, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cox and Swanson, 2013

claim: SBRT delivers high doses of radiation in a small number of fractions to the tumor lesion while minimizing radiation exposure to the surrounding tissues.
source: Stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) is a novel and relatively safe radiotherapy technique and delivers high doses of radiation in a small number of fractions to the tumor lesion while minimizing radiation exposure to the surrounding tissues (Chmura et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chmura et al., 2021

claim: Neoadjuvant radiotherapy can be applicable for inoperable breast cancer to allow an effective and sometimes more conservative surgery.
source: Currently, neoadjuvant radiotherapy can be applicable for inoperable breast cancer to allow an effective and sometimes more conservative surgery (Cardoso et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cardoso et al., 2018

claim: CDK4/6 inhibitors can sensitize breast cancer cells to radiotherapy by inhibition of DNA damage repair response, enhancement of apoptosis and blockage of cell cycle progression, and inhibition of intra-tumor cellular metabolism and angiogenesis.
source: Preclinical studies have indicated that CDK4/6 inhibitors can sensitize breast cancer cells to radiotherapy, possibly by inhibition of DNA damage repair response, enhancement of apoptosis and blockage of cell cycle progression, and inhibition of intra-tumor cellular metabolism and angiogenesis (Han et al., 2013; Pesch et al., 2020; Petroni et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to preclinical studies (Han et al., 2013; Pesch et al., 2020; Petroni et al., 2021)

claim: Radiotherapy followed by CDK4/6 inhibitors can enhance antineoplastic effects compared with their monotherapy alone or CDK4/6 inhibitors concurrent with or followed by radiotherapy.
source: A preclinical study has explored different schedules of combination of radiotherapy and CDK4/6 inhibitors in human and mouse models and demonstrated that radiotherapy followed by CDK4/6 inhibitors can enhance antineoplastic effects, compared with their monotherapy alone or CDK4/6 inhibitors concurrent with or followed by radiotherapy (Petroni et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to preclinical study (Petroni et al., 2021)

claim: The combination of CDK4/6 inhibitors and radiotherapy can lead to a satisfying overall disease control and safety based on several retrospective studies in metastatic breast cancer.
source: Moreover, the combination of CDK4/6 inhibitors and radiotherapy can lead to a satisfying overall disease control and safety based on several retrospective studies in metastatic breast cancer (Bosacki et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bosacki et al., 2021

claim: Dalpiciclib (SHR6390) is a potent selective inhibitor of CDK4/6.
source: Dalpiciclib (SHR6390) is a potent selective inhibitor of CDK4/6 and exerts synergistic antitumor effect when combined with endocrine therapy for advanced luminal breast cancer in the DAWNA-1 trials (Xu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Xu et al., 2021

claim: Dalpiciclib exerts synergistic antitumor effect when combined with endocrine therapy for advanced luminal breast cancer in the DAWNA-1 trials.
source: Dalpiciclib (SHR6390) is a potent selective inhibitor of CDK4/6 and exerts synergistic antitumor effect when combined with endocrine therapy for advanced luminal breast cancer in the DAWNA-1 trials (Xu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Xu et al., 2021

claim: The study enrolled 12 HR-positive, HER2-negative patients between November 2021 and January 2022.
source: Between November 2021 and January 2022, 12 HR-positive, HER2-negative patients were screened and recruited in the trial (Appendix 1—figure 1).
evidence: Direct statement of study enrollment data

claim: The enrolled patients had a median age of 48.5 years (range, 36–56).
source: They had a median age of 48.5 years (range, 36–56) and the median tumor size of 33.5 mm (range, 23–90) assessed by breast MRI.
evidence: Direct statement of patient demographic data

claim: The enrolled patients had a median tumor size of 33.5 mm (range, 23–90) assessed by breast MRI.
source: They had a median age of 48.5 years (range, 36–56) and the median tumor size of 33.5 mm (range, 23–90) assessed by breast MRI.
evidence: Direct statement of patient tumor size data

claim: All 12 enrolled patients completed the study treatment and surgery.
source: All 12 enrolled patients completed the study treatment and surgery.
evidence: Direct statement of study completion data

claim: Two (16.7%) of the enrolled patients achieved RCB 0-I.
source: Two (16.7%) of them achieved the RCB 0-I with the ORR of 91.7% (11/12).
evidence: Direct statement of primary endpoint results

claim: The objective response rate was 91.7% (11/12).
source: Two (16.7%) of them achieved the RCB 0-I with the ORR of 91.7% (11/12).
evidence: Direct statement of ORR results

claim: Analyses of tumor specimens showed significant increase of infiltrating T cells after treatment.
source: Analyses of tumor specimens showed significant increase of infiltrating T cells rather than alteration of PD-L1 positive immune cells.
evidence: Direct statement of biomarker analysis results

claim: Analyses of tumor specimens showed no alteration of PD-L1 positive immune cells after treatment.
source: Analyses of tumor specimens showed significant increase of infiltrating T cells rather than alteration of PD-L1 positive immune cells.
evidence: Direct statement of biomarker analysis results

claim: The most common grade 3 adverse events were neutropenia (66.7%) and leukopenia (25.0%).
source: The most common grade 3 adverse events (AEs) were neutropenia (66.7%) and leukopenia (25.0%), but no grade 4–5 AE or death occurred.
evidence: Direct statement of safety data

claim: No grade 4–5 adverse events or death occurred in the study.
source: The most common grade 3 adverse events (AEs) were neutropenia (66.7%) and leukopenia (25.0%), but no grade 4–5 AE or death occurred.
evidence: Direct statement of safety data

claim: Two (16.7%, 95% CI 3.5%–46.0%) out of 12 patients achieved RCB 0–I tumor response.
source: After the completion of study treatment, two (16.7%, 95% CI 3.5%–46.0%) out of 12 patients achieved RCB 0–I tumor response, tpCR, and PEPI 0 (Table 2).
evidence: Direct statement of primary endpoint results with confidence interval

claim: Two (16.7%, 95% CI 3.5%–46.0%) out of 12 patients achieved tpCR.
source: After the completion of study treatment, two (16.7%, 95% CI 3.5%–46.0%) out of 12 patients achieved RCB 0–I tumor response, tpCR, and PEPI 0 (Table 2).
evidence: Direct statement of pathological response results

claim: Two (16.7%, 95% CI 3.5%–46.0%) out of 12 patients achieved PEPI 0.
source: After the completion of study treatment, two (16.7%, 95% CI 3.5%–46.0%) out of 12 patients achieved RCB 0–I tumor response, tpCR, and PEPI 0 (Table 2).
evidence: Direct statement of prognostic index results

claim: Three (25.0%) patients reached bpCR.
source: There were three (25.0%) patients who reached bpCR.
evidence: Direct statement of breast pathological complete response results

claim: The study led to an ORR (as assessed by breast MRI) of 91.7% (95% CI 62.5–100%).
source: Overall, this study led to an ORR (as assessed by breast MRI) of 91.7% (95% CI 62.5–100%, Figure 1).
evidence: Direct statement of ORR results with reference to Figure 1

claim: The rate of conversion from mastectomy at baseline to breast conservation at surgery was 25.0% (95% CI 8.3%–53.9%).
source: The rate of conversion from mastectomy at baseline to breast conservation at surgery was 25.0% (95% CI 8.3%–53.9%).
evidence: Direct statement of breast conservation rate results

claim: The median Ki67 of surgical specimens for patients without pCR was 7% (range, 5–70).
source: The median Ki67 of surgical specimens for patients without pCR was 7% (range, 5–70).
evidence: Direct statement of biomarker data

claim: The most frequent grade 1–2 AEs were leukopenia (58.3%), hot flushes (50.0%), and lymphopenia (50.0%).
source: The most frequent grade 1–2 AEs were leukopenia (58.3%), hot flushes (50.0%), and lymphopenia (50.0%).
evidence: Direct statement of safety data

claim: There were no serious AEs, no therapy-related death, and no patients with dose interruption and reduction or treatment discontinuation in this population.
source: There were no serious AEs, no therapy-related death, and no patients with dose interruption and reduction or treatment discontinuation in this population.
evidence: Direct statement of safety data

claim: There was no patient with radiation-related dermatitis and skin hyperpigmentation in this population.
source: Furthermore, there was no patient with radiation-related dermatitis and skin hyperpigmentation in this population.
evidence: Direct statement of safety data

claim: There was no clinically significant deterioration in global health status, physical, role, emotional, cognitive, and social functioning in this population.
source: There was no clinically significant deterioration in global health status, physical, role, emotional, cognitive, and social functioning in this population.
evidence: Direct statement of patient-reported outcome data

claim: Treatment significantly increased the percentages of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in the tumor environment (22.9% vs 10.7%, p=0.043).
source: Compared with those in pre-treatment biopsied tissues, treatment significantly increased the percentages of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) in the tumor environment (22.9% vs 10.7%, p=0.043).
evidence: Direct statement of biomarker analysis results with statistical significance

claim: There appeared to be no significant difference in the percent of PD-L1-positive immune cells and tumor cells between the pre-treatment and post-treatment specimens.
source: IHC staining of PD-L1 revealed that there appeared to be no significant difference in the percent of PD-L1-positive immune cells and tumor cells between the pre-treatment and post-treatment specimens.
evidence: Direct statement of biomarker analysis results

claim: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy or endocrine therapy for HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer only achieves a pCR rate of ≤10%.
source: Unlike HER2-positive and triple-negative breast cancer, NCT or NET for HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer only achieves a pCR rate of ≤10% (Cortazar et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cortazar et al., 2014

claim: Neoadjuvant therapies with combination of a CDK4/6 inhibitor and letrozole led to a pCR rate of 0–3.8% and RCB 0-I rate of 6.1–7.7% in HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer patients.
source: Our study indicated that this novel therapeutic regimen achieved a pCR and RCB 0-I rate of 16.7%, while neoadjuvant therapies with combination of a CDK4/6 inhibitor and letrozole led to a pCR rate of 0–3.8% and RCB 0-I rate of 6.1–7.7% and treatment with NCT resulted in a pCR rate of 5.8–5.9% and RCB 0-I rate of 11.8–15.7% in HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer patients (Ma et al., 2017; Prat et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ma et al., 2017; Prat et al., 2020

claim: Treatment with neoadjuvant chemotherapy resulted in a pCR rate of 5.8–5.9% and RCB 0-I rate of 11.8–15.7% in HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer patients.
source: Our study indicated that this novel therapeutic regimen achieved a pCR and RCB 0-I rate of 16.7%, while neoadjuvant therapies with combination of a CDK4/6 inhibitor and letrozole led to a pCR rate of 0–3.8% and RCB 0-I rate of 6.1–7.7% and treatment with NCT resulted in a pCR rate of 5.8–5.9% and RCB 0-I rate of 11.8–15.7% in HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer patients (Ma et al., 2017; Prat et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ma et al., 2017; Prat et al., 2020

claim: pCR rate (commonly defined as ypT0/isN0) is not significantly associated with the prognosis of HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.
source: It is notable that pCR rate (commonly defined as ypT0/isN0) is not significantly associated with the prognosis of HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer (Ma et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ma et al., 2017

claim: Previous studies have revealed that NET achieves an objective response rate of approximately 60% in HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer patients.
source: In our study, treatment with the new therapeutic regimen led to 11 (91.7%) patients achieving objective responses by MRI, while previous studies have revealed that NET achieves an objective response rate of approximately 60% in HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer patients (Sella et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sella et al., 2021

claim: In the PALLET study, 14.1% of patients changed from mastectomy to breast conservation.
source: With the addition of SBRT, a slightly higher rate of patients changed from mastectomy to breast conservation compared with the PALLET study (25.0% vs 14.1%; Johnston et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Johnston et al., 2019

claim: Treatment with radiotherapy or a CDK4/6 inhibitor can enhance anti-tumor immunity in vitro.
source: Considering that treatment with radiotherapy or a CDK4/6 inhibitor can enhance anti-tumor immunity in vitro, we analyzed the impact of new neoadjuvant therapeutic regimen on alternation in biomarker expression in the numbers of TILs before and after the treatment.
evidence: Based on established preclinical knowledge

claim: Grade 3 neutropenia occurred in 84.2% of patients in the DAWNA-1 trial with combination of dalpiciclib and fulvestrant.
source: During the observation period, those patients only developed grade 1–3 AEs, including grade 3 neutropenia (66.7%), similar to that of the combination of dalpiciclib and fulvestrant in the DAWNA-1 trial (84.2%) (Xu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Xu et al., 2021

claim: There were no new AEs following therapies with radiotherapy and dalpiciclib in this population.
source: There were no new AEs following therapies with radiotherapy and dalpiciclib in this population.
evidence: Direct statement of safety data

claim: SBRT was performed every other day in the breast target lesion with a total radiation dose of 24 Gy separated by three fractions.
source: SBRT was performed every other day in the breast target lesion with a total radiation dose of 24 Gy separated by three fractions.
evidence: Direct statement of treatment protocol

claim: Patients received six cycles of a combination of oral 150 mg Dalpiciclib daily on days 1–21 of each 4-week cycle and 25 mg exemestane with a total duration of 24 weeks.
source: Within 2–4 weeks after the completion of radiotherapy, individual patients received six cycles of a combination of oral 150 mg Dalpiciclib daily on days 1–21 of each 4-week cycle and 25 mg exemestane with a total duration of 24 weeks.
evidence: Direct statement of treatment protocol

claim: Patients without menopause were also injected subcutaneously with 3.6 mg goserelin every 4 weeks.
source: Patients without menopause were also injected subcutaneously with 3.6 mg goserelin every 4 weeks.
evidence: Direct statement of treatment protocol

claim: Surgery was performed 3–5 weeks after the last dose of dalpiciclib to allow adverse event recovery.
source: Surgery was performed 3–5 weeks after the last dose of dalpiciclib to allow adverse event (AE) recovery.
evidence: Direct statement of treatment protocol

claim: SBRT with hypofractionation and higher radiation doses is more effective than conventional fractionation in triggering immune responses.
source: SBRT with hypofractionation and higher radiation doses is more effective than conventional fractionation in triggering immune responses (Gandhi et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gandhi et al., 2015

claim: Sequential neoadjuvant therapies with radiotherapy, a CDK 4/6 inhibitor, and exemestane turned non-responsive 'cold' tumors into responsive 'hot' ones.
source: Apparently, sequential neoadjuvant therapies with radiotherapy, a CDK 4/6 inhibitor, and exemestane turned non-responsive 'cold' tumors into responsive 'hot' ones.
evidence: Inferred from the observed increase in TILs

claim: The study was approved by the Institutional Review Board and Ethics Committee of Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University, according to the Declaration of Helsinki and Good Clinical Practice guidelines.
source: The study was approved by the Institutional Review Board and Ethics Committee of Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University, according to the Declaration of Helsinki and Good Clinical Practice guidelines.

source: Written informed consent was obtained from each patient.

claim: The sample size of 12 patients was determined based on clinical considerations, not statistical factors.
source: This exploratory study involves 12 patients, with the sample size determined based on clinical considerations, not statistical factors.
evidence: Direct statement of study design rationale

claim: Neoadjuvant SBRT followed by dalpiciclib and exemestane is effective and tolerable for HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.
source: Our results suggested neoadjuvant SBRT followed by dalpiciclib and exemestane is effective and tolerable and provides novel insights for the neoadjuvant treatment of HR+/HER2- breast cancer, which may be considered as a feasible option for patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.
evidence: Based on the study's primary and secondary endpoint results

claim: The sequential radiotherapy and a CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy were effective and well-tolerated.
source: The sequential radiotherapy and a CDK4/6 inhibitor plus ET were effective and well-tolerated, which could serve as a feasible option for neoadjuvant therapy for HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancers.
evidence: Based on the study's efficacy and safety results

claim: The new neoadjuvant therapeutic regimen appeared to improve the likelihood of pathological downstaging and achieve a margin-free resection, particularly for those with locally advanced and high-risk breast cancer.
source: Consequently, our new neoadjuvant therapeutic regimen appeared to improve the likelihood of pathological downstaging and achieve a margin-free resection, particularly for those with locally advanced and high-risk breast cancer.
evidence: Inferred from the observed RCB and breast conservation rates

claim: The study provides novel insights into the neoadjuvant treatment of HR+/HER2- breast cancer.
source: In conclusion, our study provides novel insights into the neoadjuvant treatment of HR+/HER2- breast cancer.
evidence: Based on the overall study findings
